you want a kind and welcoming community

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game requires creating a separate external account before playing, with no option to bypass or add one later.

citations.review_text: After 20 minutes of creating accounts and watching tedious, unskippable animations that you cannot even SILENCE, it crashed my computer.

If you love another account which will clog up your emails then this is the game for you, I am tired of having to make a new account with games. I am playing it on my STEAM account so use that not have to make another account. The game itself looks great and for what I have seen fun but I will never know. Sick of having to make new accounts for to junk up my email.

One of the worst games in User interface/user firendliness. even before starting the game it popped a window telling me i have wrong drivers. I downloaded the ones it suggested and even after that it gave me the pop up, so ihad to force it to load in DX11 through steam. 
You start the game, watch a custcene and the first thing you see is the game telling you it needs to restart. After the restart it suggests you make an account. After making the account i had to reset password 3 times (i had it right every time 100%) and then had to make a second account just for it to work because it kept telling me error 404 email and password dont match (even thought they did, literaly had it open on my phone) and guess what? you cant even skip the fuss because you cant add an account later like in 90% of modern games lol. Also had to restart like 5 times for all character customization things to load properly. 
0/10 didnt even get to gameplay because it 1. bored me to death 2. Always loaded inproperly and had to restart (yes, it palys the custcene every time you start the game and DEL being the button to skip didnt help it, had to find it every time. Who uses DEL as a skip button??)

The game gives me feeling of a cheap copy something i cant even recall of how boring it was. The only thing you could add to make it worse is in game shop, i dont know if it has one because the game literaly didnt even allow me to play it enough lol.

Do not bother with this game. Didnt even make it past the title screen because it tried to make me create an account with no option to bypass even though it said it was optional. I am tired of games wanting accounts and personal information. Immediate uninstall.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that multiplayer features are shallow, pointing out that quest progress and gathering are handled individually rather than collaboratively.

citations.review_text:
I started playing the game and quickly stopped soon after. I didn't remember why until I downloaded this game again to give it another try.

- There is no real co-op. You can get into a party with your friends and gather a specific resource together. That seems to be about it. As I remember, quest progress is not shared so if you're both on a quest to talk to a specific NPC, you both need to talk to that NPC. If a quest asks you to gather a set number of resources, you need to gather those resources individually.

- Little to no direction. If you have ADHD, do NOT play this game. The quest log is absolutely clogged with quests and always has been. There are as many MSQ quests as there are side quests and other quests, none of which seem consequential, none of which feel like they have any weight. You're going to feel somehow both over and underwhelmed -- underwhelmed by the impact the quests have and overwhelmed by their sheer number.

- Bad Map Design. I was trying to figure out how to go get a horse so I could get around faster. If you try to see where that particular quest starts, it takes you to a view of the world map and shows you. However, if you bring up your own map and try to figure out how to get there... yeah, no. Good luck with that. It only shows you a map of the current region you're in and gives you no direction on how to get where you're trying to go.

- Chest Monster: You only need to place down one chest to shove all of your stuff into. Its inventory seems to expand forever and you can craft from chests. These are good things, except for the fact that opening that chest and seeing all the stuff that you've collected at once is overwhelming. They at least gave you tabs you can click on to see only items of a specific type, but opening the chest on my home lot for the first time after awhile had me focusing ONLY on what I perceived as a mess and it took me a moment of forcing myself to focus on the UI to see the tabs.

- No Quick Stack Option: If yo…

This game has beautiful art direction and a cozy atmosphere but beneath that is a VERY shallow experience and despite being marketed as an MMO almost all meaningful progression is individual: your house, quests, relationships, storage, and unlocks. Playing with friends feels more like standing next to each other while doing separate chores than actually building something together and the game's multiplayer features remain far behind what many smaller co-op games already offer. 

And that's not even the worst part, the worst part is the cash shop which extremely predatory by all means and yeah sure it's all cosmetic whatever but I'm talking about the tactics they employ to make you spend more than you'd have to if there were upfront costs instead of a transition currency where you're left with bits after buying what you want. Or the cosmetics that you unlock via questing (like that one flaming horse) BUT NEED A PAID LICENSE TO RIDE IT, and at no point you're being told that until the end.

I wouldn't even mind the blatant anti-consumer mtx but the lack of deeper coop progression, the huge paid cosmetics emphasis at the expense of actual gameplay elements and the hacking issues that are basically left untouched since beta makes this a hard no for me. I've played this as soon as it was available and was massively disappointed and I came back now hoping that it's better. It's not, and it's not worth your time, even if it's free.

still no house sharing.... but dlc's? yes please!

grindy af and they dont want you to share and work together cause that would mean you could actually progress in a fast way without microtransactions which they dont want... just go play stardew valley at least that has a real working and fleshed out mp component without trying to get every cent you own.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the display and resolution settings as buggy, specifically reporting that resolution changes and dual-monitor window placement fail to save properly.

citations.review_text:
[h2]TL;DR: Screen resolution bug; the in-game display settings and resolution options are terrible—buggy and unfixable...[/h2]

[list]
[*]The game handles dual-monitor setups very poorly; changing the monitor selection in the game settings doesn't actually move the window—it stays stuck on the initial screen.
[*]For me, the resolution is locked to 4K 16:9 in the settings, even though I play on a 2560x1080 (UWFHD 21:9) monitor. Changing and saving the settings does nothing; the game reverts to a 4K resolution that has no relation to my actual screen...
[*]These display and resolution issues are apparently well-known; there are plenty of reports and requests for help regarding this online.
[/list]

Anyway, I spent over an hour trying to fix the problem; I had to disable my main monitor and manually force the resolution in the "GameUserSettings" file located in the AppData/Palia/... folder, then change settings in AMD software.

So, if it doesn't work for you right off the bat, seriously ask yourself:

[i]"Do I really want to spend an hour fighting with a game without being sure of the outcome or even knowing if I'll be able to play in the end?"[/i]

For me, the answer is clearly NO

One of the worst games in User interface/user firendliness. even before starting the game it popped a window telling me i have wrong drivers. I downloaded the ones it suggested and even after that it gave me the pop up, so ihad to force it to load in DX11 through steam. 
You start the game, watch a custcene and the first thing you see is the game telling you it needs to restart. After the restart it suggests you make an account. After making the account i had to reset password 3 times (i had it right every time 100%) and then had to make a second account just for it to work because it kept telling me error 404 email and password dont match (even thought they did, literaly had it open on my phone) and guess what? you cant even skip the fuss because you cant add an account later like in 90% of modern games lol. Also had to restart like 5 times for all character customization things to load properly. 
0/10 didnt even get to gameplay because it 1. bored me to death 2. Always loaded inproperly and had to restart (yes, it palys the custcene every time you start the game and DEL being the button to skip didnt help it, had to find it every time. Who uses DEL as a skip button??)

The game gives me feeling of a cheap copy something i cant even recall of how boring it was. The only thing you could add to make it worse is in game shop, i dont know if it has one because the game literaly didnt even allow me to play it enough lol.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that character customization options and clothing are restricted behind paywalls with high prices.

citations.review_text:
Obviously this review is purely based on my own perceptions, neurotic tendencies and opinions. Make up your own minds and try it for yourselves. It's just not for me.

I don't get a good vibe from the game, sadly. It feels very generic, uninspired, bland and monotonous. Nothing really stands out about it and I know I haven't played for long, but I can size up a game fairly quickly and make up my mind whether or not I will like it.

Used to enjoy games like this, where you can spend months grinding and building something. Now I shudder at the amount of time that will tick away, as I gather small amounts of materials and ingredients endlessly. It looks more like a decorating game, rather than a fleshed-out RPG.

The social side of these games doesn't interest me either, so that's another negative. I don't play online anymore and the fact this is always connected isn't a good thing in my eyes.

Looking at the shop, the game is heavily monetised and it appears that lots of content is locked behind rather large paywalls. The free options are few, so don't expect to get far without putting a hand in your pocket.

Probably a good thing I sized it up within the first hour. I'd hate to invest time into a game that wanted to bleed my wallet dry just to ride a horse or have a new piece of clothing.

It's also riddled with bugs and issues. That says a lot, when a game is very buggy yet has an expensive cash shop. They'll try to milk the hell out of it, before eventually just closing it down without a single care with regards to those who have invested lots of time and money.

I've been around long enough to see this happen with far too many games over the years.

Bullet dodged and onto the next game!

Honestly, I really liked the gameplay mechanics, this game's hunting and fishing are probably my favorite of all the games I've played so far. But accessible f2p character customization is just as important to me, if not a make-or-break. 
I would at least have liked SOME accessible and decent customizations you have to work for outside initial character creation, but everything in customization is locked behind a paywall (which, yes, this is a free game that makes money off customization than locking gameplay, but damn I would at least like a fair share of f2p earnable stuff).
If character customization is just a bonus for you though, ignore my review.

Almost every cosmetic equals out to about $23 USD so if you wanted custom clothing, a custom pet and some custom tools you are spending close to $100 USD just so that you can look at your character and be a bit happier. Don't get me wrong I'd be glad to pay for cosmetics, but at such a steep price? I got about halfway through the tutorial, it's very slow and methodic but that's not technically bad I just wish I could enjoy more about the world during that, not much to see though unless you plan to spend a lot of money.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that character creation options are minimal and lack variety for free players.

citations.review_text: It feels like someone tried building an entire game out of a crafting mini-game. Controls and UI are surprisingly clunky for something that's been out for a few years. Character customization is disappointing. Someone literally thought: Let's create a world populated by diverse, unique, highly customized elven NPCs with a variety of body shapes, skin colors, unique facial features... and we'll let the players be humans with the same exact body and three skin color choices. Apparently, Palia sold out to Daybreak Games, and Daybreak is a subsidiary of Enad Global 7 which is a Swedish holding company that's been hoovering up game studios, sucking value from them, and then barely maintaining the acquired games while adding massive cash shops. It's too bad, it was nice playing an RPG without a health or mana bar for a minute.

I've been playing this game since it released in closed beta, my steam hours don't reflect how many hours I actually have in this game as I was playing it before it came to steam. I really liked it at first, until they started pushing paid cosmetic bundles and then it really just left a bad taste in my mouth. I'll start by saying that I fully acknowledge that this game is free-to-play, and that the Devs need to make their money somehow. I don't mind paid cosmetics or battle passes in games, and if I like a game enough I am obviously going to support it as most people do too. But there's something that very much bothers me about a game that does absolutely nothing to update it's base character customization options as it grows, especially in a game where customization, crafting and building are some of the key points, while continuing to push out load after load of paid for cosmetics that on top of it are quite expensive. I guess it would be more okay if Palia had an armor or clothing crafting system, if there were more options to learn and to access for free instead of just the very minimal options offered to you at the start of the game, but it doesn't, so your character just feels like the one thing in the world that's entirely flavorless and without personality. Unless you pay 40$ to not look like a thumb.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features housing customization and decoration systems.

citations.review_text:
Don't let my 4 hours playtime fool you, I have over 400 hours on my other account. I just felt like posting another review. This game is something I have been wanting for years. It's so cozy, yet there is always something to do. I really like that you can decide whether you want to participate in certain aspects of the game. For example, if you don't like hunting, you can just buy the stuff you may need from the guy that hunts. You can then just make money by doing something you DO like. You can just fish for eternity if you want and buy all the stuff you wouldn't get by fishing. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ sick. 

Love decorating my own plot, and how detailed you can get. 
So cool how you can also tour other people's plots for inspiration, love that feature!

What I maybe love most about this game, is how much the devs care about it. They listen to what their players want, and I feel like that's kind of rare nowadays. 
I was yearning for horses (or other mounts) and I know other people were as well. And what got added a few months back? Thats right. Horses.

The only part I don't really like is the ability to play with your friends. It is ofcourse a MMO, and I love seeing other players just running about and doing  their own thing. I just wish there were more options to REALLY play together with your friends. Right now it just feels like you're both kind of doing your own thing together, instead of really doing something together. If you know what I mean.

But to make a long story short, I totally recommend this game.

Honestly a great game with lots to do. You can put hundreds of hours into this game with quests, fishing, foraging, farming, mining, etc. Romance included but it could be better, really its just dialogue but I'd like something a bit more interactive. Housing customization is amazing and super cozy. The recent Ranching addition is slightly confusing and requires regular logins but still cute and fun. Elderwoods map started to get too complex and grindy for me personally, but I think it's good for those with more commitment to the game. Overall this is an amazing free game worth trying.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game's initial pacing as very slow.

citations.review_text: So far I've played about 10 hours, and I've really enjoyed the game, I will admit though that it is very slow at first so try to keep that in mind and give it a little bit to reel you in. Once you get the hang of the mechanics (fishing, bug catching, gardening, foraging, mining, etc.) it becomes much easier. Its very relaxing and so far I haven't had any issues with anyone in game. I highly recommend using the Wiki for it. <3 I am kinda excited to see where this goes and I'm now ready to actually spend some real money on it. <3
The game is cute and cozy but very slow paced. I played for 3 hours and it still felt like the tutorial. Probably a wonderful game for younger players.

citations.review_text: At first seemed a nice sandboxish game UNTIL I checked out the store. How on gods greed sorry green earth are the skins almost 30 or 20ish bucks idk no hate to whoever plays this but it feels like a game catered for disney adults with adult money...its playable without buying anything though.

I'm new to the game, tbh I would like to love the game but I've noticed some issues.

I keep on getting crashes every 5-10 mins, like others. I thought it had something to do with my driver but after updating and reinstalling it the same issue persist. I'm not sure if this is a recent update issue but so far... not so very fun.

I also checked out the IAPs of the game and must say that it feels like such a money grabber as you look at it. If I remember correctly I opened the IAPs and there was a skin for 60€? now THats a lot of money that I will not be spending, especially on a skin.

I could already tell from playing the amount that I have so far that this game will have a FOMO issue and the constant grinding (farming) is also going to be an issue.

It still needs a decent amount of work, Crashes and optimization needs attention. Other than that, it's been good. Should be pretty lit in 5-10 years. My only real compliant is store items are a bit overpriced for what the game currently offers. That, and first-time setup is a real pain - lots of black screens, shader loadings, etc.

Edit: This game has given me the feeling I first had when playing BOTW, Warframe, and SWTOR. It's great, it's got amazing potential, they just need to make sure they're providing a good balance of player-experience and profit so they can stay afloat. The $30 outfits are bit insane, yet I would pay $30 to buy this Free-To-Play game at the same time, due to it's vast content. I imagine I will be sinking in many hundreds of hours into this game.

claims.claim: The game features cosmetic items and premium currency packs that reviewers describe as overly expensive.

citations.review_text:
Played this first on my Nintendo Switch before moving to PC. It’s such a cozy and relaxing game, though I personally enjoy it more as a solo experience since co-op can get a bit laggy at times.

One thing I appreciate is that you can fully enjoy the game without spending money on packs, although the cosmetics and bundles can feel pretty pricey depending on your budget. Of course, everyone has their own way of exploring and supporting a game.

Overall, Palia is a great game with a charming atmosphere. My only wish is for the storage limit to expand beyond 10,000 items. I know furniture storage is unlimited, but regular storage still fills up pretty quickly.

Look...I really wanted to love this game but i cant get over the cost of cosmetics($12-25 each). I know the team works hard but having a cosmetic cost so much with no way to work toward those cosmetics for free is a real downer for me. I never change my characters clothes cause none of the free stuff outside of what i have already picked fits my character.  everything fun looking is locked behind a paywall. 

Really feel the team should take a page out of Warframes book. 

Also  cant recycle furtiture...I spend all this time grinding for mats i should get stuff back for it but the dev team really expects you to store it or throw it away. Heck you cant even trade it to friends!

This game does not respect the players time.  If you want a community game that respects your time, Play Spirit Crossing. At least everything is free and it feels like the devs care and respect the players time.

I have so far enjoyed playing Palia. The story line so far has got me hooked and curious to see where it goes! I love open world games so this is perfect for that. The good but no so good part is I sit and play the game for hours upon hours!! I would have also much preferred alternative ways to get Palia coins such as a reasonably priced monthly membership or at least more options in regards to the amount of coins you can buy. I just feel as though the price for the amount of Palia coins you would get is ridiculous, as the items in the shop you would then use the Palia coins to purchase are expensive (for the good stuff anyway), so you buying the pack to get 850 coins or buying 425 coins will not get you very far at all. That is my only complaint other than that the game is super fun and very enjoyable to play! I have so far been playing for a week so we shall see if my opinion stays the same?....

gameplay is fun and easy to understand. story is engaging and interesting, and i love how every NPC has their own personality. leveling up skills can be tedious but if you're patient it's no big deal. my only real complaint is the price of Palia coins--far too high a price for what feels like very little in-game currency, in my opinion. get your bag devs, but dang. give us poorer gamers a break. ;-; we like cute stuff for our characters, too! lol 

anyway, the visuals are phenomenal and i love the artstyle in this game. the colors are vibrant and i do love the more cartoony aspects. have noticed a few issues with dialogue (like weird player responses that don't exactly align with what the character has said/asked (a character (i won't say who as not to spoil it) asked me what i wanted on my congee and all i could respond with was what i thought her congee toppings said about her, for example, but the next dialogue she asked me again what i wanted and i was able to say), or repeated dialogue (Hekla said something twice in one dialogue tree)), but it's not so off-putting that it takes away from the gameplay. just minor formatting mistakes. 

i highly recommend this game to anyone who enjoys the "cozy" genre. it's fun and cute and i think you'll have a good time. if you like Stardew Valley or Starsand Island (two of my other favorites), you'll enjoy this game.

no comment on the MMO aspect as i tend to play alone, but i'm sure it's extra fun with friends. <:

Love,
Reth's future wife. 

ehehehehehehehehe.

I wish I could give a neutral review. It's a free game and decorating your lot is fun, but tbh I spend all my time running around following quests that involve running back and forth over massive maps and by the time I'm done playing don't have much to show for it and have forgotten what I even was wanting to do. 70 hours in and I'm still on the basic quests.  

I would say it's a fun game to pick up when you're bored with other games, the maps are very pretty though barren. The cost of outfits is way too expensive especially compared to similar games, the only thing I've bought is the backdrops which are quite pretty. 

I'd say, sure play it since it's free, but don't expect too much, it's pretty much a walking game with crafting and decorating if you eventually accumulate enough money to buy some recipes for the more interesting furniture and buildings 
I do think the game still has potential if they flesh out the world a bit more and make it feel more alive. The characters are quite charming and it is very pretty.

claims.claim: Players describe visual glitches where NPCs clip or lag halfway into the ground.

citations.review_text: I am addicted. I picked this up barely a week ago, and I've played this every chance I've gotten. If you like cozy games, you'd definitely like this! Once you get tired of leveling up your regular skills, there are minigames you can play. I haven't spent any time decorating my house, but I'm looking forward to it! If you're looking for a new cozy farming game, definitely check this out! Any paid features are cosmetic, so this is not pay-to-win. There are a few bugs, such as villagers clipped halfway into the ground or it being hard to interact with certain objects. I haven't come across any game-breaking bugs, so kudos. If you get motion-sick easily (like I do), I turned off all the screen shake settings and turned on fixed point which definitely helps. The only time I started getting motion sick again was in close quarters (maze-like structures), and I wished I could zoom the camera out. Other than that, great game! Can't wait to see how this grows!

I have played this game on PS5 and on PC. It really is a cute little game. It has all aspects: Mining, Hunting, Gathering, Fishing, Planting Crops, Tending to animals, Building furniture, Organizing/decorating your plot, Cooking,  and Catching bugs. I’m only 82 hours into Palia, but it has already become one of those games where I log in thinking, “I’ll just play for an hour…” and suddenly several hours have disappeared. 😂

I absolutely love collecting, looting, gathering and being rewarded for exploring and doing things. Farming games have always been my thing, and Palia gives me a little bit of everything I enjoy: farming, crafting, gathering resources, fishing, decorating, exploring, completing quests… there is always something to do.

But what really surprised me is how much I enjoy the online aspect. I’ve already met some genuinely lovely people, and teamwork actually feels important here. Instead of competing for everything, there are so many moments where working together benefits everyone – and I love that.

It’s cozy without feeling empty, relaxing without becoming boring, and there’s always another little goal waiting for me.

Palia is simply a game I genuinely enjoy coming back to. I log in, start doing “one quick thing”… and somehow I’m still there hours later.

82 hours so far – and definitely many more to come. 💚
vary cozy, a lot to do, map it divided in to sections so the game is a lot bigger then you think. i really like the community as well.

I am addicted. I picked this up barely a week ago, and I've played this every chance I've gotten. If you like cozy games, you'd definitely like this! Once you get tired of leveling up your regular skills, there are minigames you can play. I haven't spent any time decorating my house, but I'm looking forward to it! If you're looking for a new cozy farming game, definitely check this out! Any paid features are cosmetic, so this is not pay-to-win. There are a few bugs, such as villagers clipped halfway into the ground or it being hard to interact with certain objects. I haven't come across any game-breaking bugs, so kudos. If you get motion-sick easily (like I do), I turned off all the screen shake settings and turned on fixed point which definitely helps. The only time I started getting motion sick again was in close quarters (maze-like structures), and I wished I could zoom the camera out. Other than that, great game! Can't wait to see how this grows!

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features cosmetic items and outfits in the premium shop that are expensive.

citations.review_text: I have 730+ hours of play. I started a few years back when Palia had only a few npcs to interact with, but I had so much fun exploring the world and doing activities with other players. At this point, I have all the quests completed and most of the achievements done, but I kept coming back for enjoyable time. However, starting about a year ago, when this game became overpopular, something happened to the devs - they just stopped caring. Now all I see when logging in is a new expensive set of cosmetics or a paid path if you really want cool things, not trash. As many already said, instead of fixing insane amount of bugs, they just keep pushing new paid items or really stupid board bundles that you have to work hard for just to receive another portion of trash. I've been waiting so long for this game to get better, but it only got worse. Finally, I just uninstalled it. To be fair, I did purchase a lot of cosmetics in the beginning to support the devs since the game is free, but at this point, I regret each of the purchase.

Considering it's in EA and already has about a hundred plus hours of content I'm looking forward to seeing this in it's final form. Great cozy game, lot's of things to do, somewhat grindy, MTX are too expensive, some bugs and glitches, but it's addicting and fun and I lose time like crazy when I play. Wish the party/community/social aspects were more fleshed out and the game had more built-in mini games and events to participate in, but the seasonal events and bundle boards are always fun to grind out.

a bit grindy for item drops as all MMOs are, but it's cozier and easier to get help from others with a request system and buffs for cooperation. i used to use the Palia launcher before switching to steam, so i have a LOT more hours in than is displayed here. i've been wanting mounts for ages and they finally delivered, and i couldn't be more pleased with how it turned out given the ranching system, too.

my biggest gripe with the game is its premium store and how expensive everything is. sure, it's just cosmetics, but spending over $30 on premium currency for a single item is insane... the only thing worth spending money on is Zeki's Loyalty Club if you're a regular player, which gives you a steep discount in exchange for delayed gratification.

i also have issue with the number of mf TYPOS and misspellings that can be found in the game's dialogue! please, hire someone to proofread it first!!

other than that, nice game, beautiful music... good time with friends and strangers alike.

Palia is my soulmate of the game world. Cozy, play at your own pace, and keeps me busy.

Here are my thoughts more in depth:

-House building and decorating is unmatched, however I wish more house pieces were able to connect to each other.

- Free to play and your choice to purchase from the premium shop does not hinder your ability to advance in the game which is great for those who don't or can't spend money.
          - I will say, the premium shop is excessively expensive and the fact that single pieces of clothing can't be purchased without purchasing the entire outfit has always been absurd to me.

- I love the interactions with the villagers and all their different personalities. The downfall to this however is their dialogue gets SUPER repetitive especially after you've maxed out the friendships and romance.

- I ADORE the map and the open world exploration. There are so many creatures to find and random activities to do in each of the areas.
          - I will say though, the new expansion of the Royal Highlands was kind of disappointing to me. It took me so long to fully explore the Elderwood and get my bearings in that area, but the Royal Highlands didn't really add much in my opinion and it was super easy to get through despite it being the biggest exploration area. (Crab Wars helped me like the Royal Highlands more)

- There is ALWAYS something to do in this game and it keeps me locked in for HOURS upon hours.

- I'm addicted to Hotpot.

- When a new update comes out the new main story quests take me all of 30 minutes to complete which is a little sad. I like doing the story quests more than anything else because it gives me something to actually work towards, and now after being caught up with everything it's kind of a let down. I will say it did take a long time to get caught up with the main story when I first started playing the game, but I still wish more of the story was added in the updates.

- I can't get hurt. I'm not the kind of person who pla…

Stardew Valley meets Animal Crossing as an MMO. Probably the best cozy game experience I've had since the pandemic-fueled New Horizon craze. I genuninely adore this game. Has some fun co-op activities and generally satisfying game systems and a super charming cast of villagers. The world is surprisingly beautiful for its simplified style, owing to the gorgeous lighting and skyboxes and tight artistic vision. The music is phenomenal. It does feel like the potential is somewhat hamstrung by the Switch (1) support, if rumours of the neglected rain/weather system truly is due to the limitations of the Switch.

I just wish the individual cosmetic items in the (optional) in game store were cheaper, to better justify spending and supporting the team. There is no game where €20-30 outfit price-tags are justified. I want to feel good about regularly spending to support the creators and upkeep of this otherwise free game, but the pricing makes that less frequent as I get decision paralysis due to the steep prices.

Thankfully the packs are good value, but I don't see myself making additional purchases outside of those. Other than that, the game is an 11/10 for me.

I really want to like this game, it has good bones, but has a few aspects that completely sour the experience:
- The late game quickly becomes incredibly grindy and many of the late game challenges are heavily dependent on RNG
- Story updates are few and far between with minimal additional content. Expect only a few hours of new quests a year
- Cosmetics are quite pricey (even by free-to-play game standards) and the game is slowly moving towards pay-to-win content
- If you're unlucky bugs can completely cripple your account. I'm stuck on the main story quest and support is unwilling / unable to help outside completely resetting my account with 100s of hours on it.

Great player community, cute animals, building/decorating, fun story lines. What more could you want from a free cozy mmo? Are there bugs? Yup. Do you complain about them all the time? Yes. Does it keep you from coming back the next day? Nope. Only negative is the cosmetics have gotten really expensive.

The other players are kind, and there is always someone nearby who is happy to help or answer questions for beginners (and ppl who are bad at games like me... haha), and plenty to do even when you're not a beginner. It’s amazing that this game is free. There’s so much to do: quests, NPC relationship building, bug/fish/gem collection, crafting/building, decorating, cooking, etc. the list goes on! This is the nicest MMO community I’ve experienced as well. Pretty much everyone is welcoming and helpful, and the developers work to keep it this way. I love that the game is designed to reward working together, but you can do things solo as well. Honestly I don’t have anything negative to say about this game. It is perfect for those of us who love cozy games!

10/10. I have a horse called Banjo and Eshe still doesn’t like me.

I didn’t get into Palia the first time I played it. Nearly 200 hours later, I have a strict ranching routine, dress as a cowboy, own a horse called Banjo, and have a standing appointment with Reth at 4am round the back of Jel’s shop.

So that’s going well.

Palia is wholesome, laid-back and properly cosy. It has that same feeling as Stardew Valley, a little world of its own that you can disappear into for a few hours. The community is lovely without being overbearing, and the biggest crisis you’ll face is missing the two-hour window to catch a Rainbow Butterfly because you were busy having an intense game of Spam Pot.

It’s perfectly acceptable to take three weeks to finish a quest because you ran out of inventory space picking up unopened oysters. There’s no rush. You can fish, farm, hunt, mine, romance people, hoard an unreasonable amount of money or just wander about doing whatever takes your fancy.

My house is an absolute mess because apparently decorating is less important than accumulating wealth. My best friend is a K-pop princess and every time we play together we perform a k-pop routine until someone else joins in. I've walked for a good half hours worth of real time on horse back with total strangers to help someone else complete the mission that gets them the horse, more than once. Eshe still doesn’t like me, despite my best efforts.

And the best bit? It’s free. Obviously there are cosmetics you can buy, because the developers presumably enjoy having electricity and food. They’ve got to make money somehow.

It’s peaceful, pretty and genuinely lovely to spend time in.

Anyway, I’m off to see Reth at 4am.

Eshe won't approve.

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that the game receives regular updates and new content additions.

citations.review_text: I adore this game. I love that you can play at your own pace. They are constantly adding new things. and I can't wait till they add more to the story.

I have played this game for less than a month, and have put in just under 130hrs. I adore this game, there's tons of story, the core gameplay loop is mega fun, it looks gorgeous, and the characters are super interesting and cute! It is also very much a social game, though you can do much solo. This game has helped me be more social while still respecting my anxieties around it. My only complaints are that there are tons of in-game purchases that make the game much easier and/or far cuter, and that it triggers my carpal tunnel badly (running, etc. However, that is definitely a me issue! Auto-run and some other features do help but it's not a cure-all). The community is great overall (few issues, and you can block players that are. There are bugs, and the in game news is not as communicative as the official discord (for example, the bug lures causing crashes for a period of time was communicated on discord, but not in in-game news leading to people unknowingly using them). It does appear the game also gets frequent updates with new content and challenges. It does also have some element of real time events (in-game monthly 'Maji Market' or seasonal bulletin board quests and weekly wants/gifts from characters!).

I mean, I don't sink 121 hours into a game that I don't like. Palia scratches the cozy game & MMO itch really well. The updates are incredible, and you get so much content for free that other developers would easily charge for. The devs are also very communicative and listen to the community. 

It can be a bit slow, especially if you're a more quest-motivated person, but I don't find it to be too bad.

This game has brought so many wonderful people into my life. I would absolutely recommend it.

I can’t believe this a free game. it is so much fun, so much to do, 1300 hours in and I’m not running out of steam anytime soon. love the lore. 

I have met so many friends playing this game. There are nearly monthly updates with new content. and it’s still technically in beta. yes, there can be bugs, especially on patch day, but again: a free game. and the devs work hard to fix problems. they have fixed a couple issues for me in a very timely manner. and they listen to player feedback. 

love you palia devs <3

Been playing everyday for about a year and Palia has easily become my #1 favorite game! Everything from the quests, lore, community, and frequent patches + updates they put out for us, I never get bored and there's always something for me to enjoy doing. It's great for solo play and even better with others. Just all around super fun, rewarding, and it has become my happy place haha. Highest recommendation!

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the opening phase of the game as an intense grind with a lack of clear instructions or direction for new players.

citations.review_text:
So fair warning, this review is coming from a new player (Started less than 2 months ago w/ <200 hours) who got into this game after seeing videos of the mounts and farm animals with breedable cosmetic and non cosmetic traits  and the content surrounding it. As a die hard horse girl from the time I could walk, I have searched for the perfect horse game that has that "pick up and play" feel with a good community. 

Now saying all that, this is not a horse game and do not expect that, but if you are willing to sacrifice the realistic horse/animal aspect of a game this fantasy MMO will scratch that itch. Not in the satisfying way that this game absolutely can and should, but I would safely say it could replace a lot of player's daily games until that game comes around.

Here is my short list of grievances:
1. Start of game is an absolute grind-fest and lack of direction is a real issue. Thankfully the community has helped with this so asking for help is very easy and there are walkthroughs posted by multiple people for anything you have trouble with.

2. Lack of instruction/direction by itself. It's important to list this as it's own point because tutorials literally guide players on how to play your game, and you CANNOT just give them half the instructions and let them guess the rest. i.e. Placing one of each cooking station down and thinking you can cook whatever you want now when in reality, some recipes require duplicates of certain stations. The current set up/indicator does not work new players trying to figure things out.

3. Reasonable Storage/Capacity limits. Now again, I'm a new player who just unlocked paladian storage chests, so I'm not feeling squeezed there at the moment (however I can definitely see where later on down the line when I start decorating my plot and getting into money making etc. that there will need to be some management on my own hoarding tendencies to stay happy there).  My REAL issue with this game is HOW ARE YOU GOING TO CAP O…

It took a while to get the hang of the whole game.but the community is so nice and strong that the struggles were fun and never too tiring. If you grind enought you get to have cool looking clothes and fun things which i like. I hated the limited chest space before ,but now i like how it forces you to use your items and never keep much so you have to go out more often. The events are fun and the whole hunting and gardening systems are my favourite ! lovely game.
